neighbours.label: the sub-global place or scope (campus, county, region, state) that bounds a superlative or 'first' claim ('the tallest building on [campus]', 'the best in the [region]'); the + pole takes the global bounds 'world' / 'ever'
fire: The library is the oldest building on campus.
They make the finest cheese in the county.
It became the largest hospital in the region.
This is the busiest airport in the state.
She owns the biggest farm in the valley.
It was the first cinema in the district.
He coached the strongest team in the league.
That is the highest waterfall in the province.
quiet: The library is the oldest building in the world.
They make cheese in the county every spring.
It became the largest hospital ever built.
The airport in the state capital closed early.
She walked across the valley before noon.
The cinema in the district shows old films.
He coached a team in the league for years.
It is the highest waterfall on Earth.

notes: Probes: superlative + campus 0.45, county 0.37, region 0.25, Asia 0.23, Dublin 0.05; 'in the world' 0.04; the same place words without a superlative under 0.02. The two poles are the two sides of one distinction: local versus global bound of a superlative.
